rv.q: Adapted and directed by Ed Rutherford, the stage version has strong world-building and creative visuals, but the character arcs and themes feel underdeveloped.
In its world premiere, Chicago theatergoers get a promising new theatrical offering for fans of the Harry Potter series.
A Shadow Bright and Burning, in spirit and aesthetic appeal, is overall a welcome return to production for the company after being on hiatus for the past couple of years.
Overall, I like this play and recommend it for a fun time.
But when the script does not work as well as intended, then a clever fantasy does not have the impact that it should.

cn.t: This fantasy adaptation earns praise for its energetic heroine and imaginative Victorian magical world, with critics commending the production's ambition in bringing Henrietta Howell's sorcerer journey to the stage.
